_meta.indication: Treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients 6 years of age and older

pivotal_trials.phase: Adequate and well-controlled 18-month randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study
pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study; patients randomized 2:1 to givinostat or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: 179 male ambulant DMD patients aged 6 years and older on stable concomitant steroids
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Month 18 in the time to climb four stairs (4SC) in the target population (baseline vastus lateralis muscle fat fraction >5% and <=30% by MRS)
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant less worsening in 4SC time with givinostat (1.25 sec) vs placebo (3.03 sec); treatment difference -1.78 seconds, p = 0.037

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%): diarrhea (37% vs 20% placebo), abdominal pain (34% vs 25%), thrombocytopenia (33% vs 0%), nausea/vomiting (32% vs 18%), hypertriglyceridemia (23% vs 7%), pyrexia (13% vs 8%). Thrombocytopenia is dose-related.
target_moa: Zinc-dependent histone deacetylase (HDAC) class I and II inhibitor; an orally active hydroxamic acid derivative
modality: Small molecule (orally active hydroxamic acid derivative HDAC inhibitor)

advisory_committee.vote: Advisory Committee: Not applicable (no advisory committee convened)

orphan_indication.text: Granted orphan drug designation for treatment of DMD on April 12, 2013

citations.quote: We also inform you that you have been granted a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher, as provided under section 529 of the FDCA.

summary.text: Duvyzat (givinostat) received a traditional (full) approval under a Priority review of NDA 217865, based on a single adequate and well-controlled study plus confirmatory evidence; it holds orphan drug designation for DMD and was granted a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher.

citations.quote: Therefore, for this rare disease with unmet medical need, the single adequate and well-controlled study plus confirmatory evidence provide substantial evidence of effectiveness for givinostat in the treatment of DMD in patients 6 years and older.
